clue.text: King and Queen soon upset God

parts.note: R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

indicators.note: upset means the letters of soon are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A royal couple are told the deity will shortly be overthrown.
explanation.walkthrough: R for Regina is the usual crossword queen; the god's name follows the two royal letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Kronos is the Titan of Greek myth, father of Zeus, so a deity in the classical pantheon.

clue.text: Joint protection once called in revolutionary gang

indicators.note: in places the former-name word inside the other piece
revolutionary means turned round, so the gang word is reversed

parts.note: née marks a former or maiden name

explanation.surface: A revolutionary gang once used a name for their protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A kneecap is the patella, the bone that shields the knee joint at the front.

clue.text: Weaselly individual wanders about naked

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outer layer, so first and last letters go

parts.note: someone who totters wanders about unsteadily

explanation.surface: A shifty character roams around with no clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weaselly' sounds like a slur on character; it means of the weasel family.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter belongs to the mustelids, the weasel family, so it is a weasel-like animal.

clue.text: Huge amount of work stopping no one company rising

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the work word goes inside
rising in a down clue means read upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: to till is to work the soil

explanation.surface: A vast amount of labour halts a nobody's firm as it grows.
explanation.definitionFit: An octillion is ten to the power of twenty-seven, an enormous number.

clue.text: Self-confident idiot's dreadfully rude

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests rude is badly mangled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cocky fool is said to be appallingly impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after idiot reads as 'is' and only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An assured person has poise and certainty in their own abilities, a synonym for self-confident.

clue.text: Continental area has sufficient power to support French island

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means coming below, so this piece follows

parts.note: can means is able, having enough power to do something

explanation.surface: A region strong enough to prop up an island belonging to France.
explanation.definitionFit: African means belonging to Africa, one of the world's continents.

clue.text: What may cross boundaries for audience in particular way of writing?

indicators.note: for audience means as heard by listeners, so a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps for climbing over a field fence or wall

explanation.surface: A question about a prose manner that transcends limits for its readers.
explanation.definitionFit: A style is an author's characteristic manner of expression in prose.

clue.text: Masseur is initially expected to put on protective coat

parts.note: a masseur rubs the body, so is a rubber

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of expected is used

explanation.surface: A massage therapist is told to wear a protective coat first.
explanation.definitionFit: To rubberise is to treat or coat a material with rubber, giving a protective layer.

clue.text: Show disapproval about being detained by boring thing one cannot name

indicators.note: being detained by means held inside the other piece
about means turned round, so the jeer is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone jeers on being held up by a tedious nameless gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: Doobry is British colloquial for a whatsit, an object whose name escapes you.
explanation.definitionFit: A doobry is a thingamajig, a placeholder word for something whose name is forgotten.

clue.text: Build up credit union's leader with great coverage

indicators.note: coverage means the great word wraps around the other pieces
leader means the first letter of union is used

explanation.surface: A credit union's chief accumulates funds, with a big insurance policy.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrue is to accumulate over time, as interest does in an account.

clue.text: Vehicle, say, in track event getting withdrawn

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
withdrawn here means drawn back, so the track event word is read in reverse

parts.note: a race is an event on the track

explanation.surface: Someone describes a vehicle being pulled out of a race at a track meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate car is a type of car with a long body and rear door, i.e. a kind of motor vehicle.

clue.text: Lout's two children almost going head-to-head

indicators.note: the first boy is turned round so that its head, the B, meets the head of the second boy

parts.note: the first of the two boys the clue's 'two children' gives

indicators.note: almost means the second boy loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A hooligan is two kids who keep butting heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two children' gives BOY twice: the first is turned round and the second shortened so the two B's, their heads, touch. Yobbo is British slang for a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: Yobbo is British slang for a rowdy, aggressive young man, a near synonym of hooligan.

clue.text: Sing part of barcarolle

indicators.note: part of means the answer is a run of letters lying inside barcarolle

explanation.surface: An instruction to sing a section of a gondolier's song.
explanation.definitionFit: To carol is to sing joyfully, especially festive songs, so it is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Terrible noise listener said is one to avoid?

parts.note: a racket is a loud din

indicators.note: said means the piece is spoken, so we write a spelling that sounds like it

explanation.surface: Someone complains of an awful din and suggests whose company to shun.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a crook running a racket is a person best given a wide berth.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer is a gangster running illegal schemes, someone sensible people steer clear of.

clue.text: American embroiled in public relations row is kind of sweet

indicators.note: embroiled in means caught up inside, so one letter goes within the others

explanation.surface: A US citizen caught in a PR spat, oddly described as a type of confection.
explanation.definitionFit: A praline is a confection of nuts boiled in sugar, a type of candy.

clue.text: Sweetener upset team following a dispute

indicators.note: following means the rearranged team comes after
upset means the letters of team are tipped over and reordered

explanation.surface: A disgruntled sports side reacts after an argument with a sugar substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspartame is an artificial, low-calorie sugar substitute used in diet drinks.

clue.text: Recent arrival's drunk a lot of beer and a lot of wine

indicators.note: drunk suggests letters that stagger about into a new order
a lot of means most but not all of beer is used, dropping its final letter
again most of wine is kept, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A newcomer has got tipsy on plenty of ale and plenty of vino.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after the definition reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A newbie is a novice newly joined to a group, i.e. a newcomer.

clue.text: Malware gets rid of evidence of underground activity?

parts.note: a worm is a self-spreading computer virus
to cast is to shed or throw off

explanation.surface: Malicious software wipes the traces of a covert operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground activity' suggests espionage or resistance; it is earthworms burrowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Wormcasts are the coiled mounds of earth left by burrowing worms, signs of activity below the soil.

clue.text: Author's negative response is reflected in titular character

indicators.note: reflected means turned back as in a mirror, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the setter, as author, refers to their own possession as my

explanation.surface: A writer's refusal echoes in the character who gives the book its title.
explanation.definitionFit: An eponym is the person after whom something is named, such as a title character like Hamlet.

clue.text: Sprinkle items on ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the letters are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: An instruction to scatter things over the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like soil; it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: To moisten is to make slightly wet, as sprinkling water does.

clue.text: Flower in beer garden's half gone to seed

indicators.note: gone to seed means run to ruin, so the letters are jumbled
half means only the first three of garden's six letters are kept

parts.note: the word garden, half of which is kept

explanation.surface: A bloom in a pub garden that has half run wild.
explanation.definitionFit: A gerbera is a daisy-like plant grown for its bright blooms, an example of a flower.

clue.text: School article about singular individual doing readings

indicators.note: about means around, so the other pieces surround the singular letter

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales

explanation.surface: A school grammar point about a single person who reads aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Readings' sounds literary; it means meter readings.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasman is the utility worker who reads household gas meters.

clue.text: Exacting short-term drills start off aerobic exercise

indicators.note: start off means only the first letter of aerobic is used
drills means bores into, so the shortened word goes inside the others

parts.note: to exercise a right is to use it

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the word term, before it is shortened

explanation.surface: A demanding short course of drills begins with aerobic workouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means severe and strict, so demanding in a stern way.

clue.text: Salvation Army doctrine mainly dedicated to religious use

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a credo is a statement of belief

explanation.surface: The Salvation Army's creed is largely given over to faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacred describes things consecrated or holy, set apart for worship.

clue.text: Type of clue receiving much credit in word puzzles

indicators.note: receiving means the clue type takes another piece inside it

parts.note: an across clue is one type of crossword clue

indicators.note: much means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A clue type that earns a lot of praise in puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: On tick means on credit in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrostics are puzzles in which initial letters of lines spell out a word, a kind of word game.

clue.text: School mom dumps married idiot in New York

indicators.note: dumps means throws out, so one letter is removed from mom

explanation.surface: A school mother leaves her husband for a fool in Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In New York' marks the word as American slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmo is US slang, from Yiddish, for a stupid or contemptible person.

clue.text: Copper's bored by following his usual restraint

indicators.note: bored by means pierced by, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, with the 's kept
ff. is the abbreviation for following pages

explanation.surface: A police officer stuck on routine reaches for the usual handcuffs.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper is British slang for a police officer, so 'his usual restraint' points to the policeman's handcuffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuffs are handcuffs, the standard device police use to restrain suspects.

clue.text: Produce attack to seal game

indicators.note: to seal means to enclose, so the game goes inside

parts.note: a fit is a sudden attack, as of coughing

explanation.surface: An assault designed to clinch the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit can mean produce in general, the yield of the land.

clue.text: Last of joint method deleting application

indicators.note: deleting means the application letters are removed from the method word

parts.note: an approach is a way of doing something
an app is a software application

explanation.surface: A procedure for cutting the final part of a joint out of software.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like a body joint or a cut of meat; it is a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A roach is slang for the butt end of a cannabis cigarette, the last bit left.

clue.text: To instil mortal fear, stun suspect to begin with

indicators.note: mortal, as in deadly, signals the words are destroyed and rebuilt in a new order
to begin with means only the opening letter of suspect is used

explanation.surface: A villain aims to strike deathly terror and shock a suspect from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mortal fear' reads as one phrase, but mortal is the anagram signal and fear is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To transfuse is to permeate or infuse something, figuratively to pass a quality into it.

clue.text: Drop off and admit having stopped working earlier

indicators.note: earlier means the stopped-working piece comes before the other

parts.note: a machine that has died has stopped working
to own something is to admit it

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to dozing off after the engine had failed.
explanation.definitionFit: To die down is to decline or abate, so it means the same as dropping off in intensity.

clue.text: Set about limiting firm's cause for complaint?

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing, so the scrambled word holds the other inside
about suggests the letters of Set are moved around

parts.note: set means firm, as a jelly sets

explanation.surface: Someone starts to restrict a company's grievance procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after firm reads as 'is'. The question mark flags the pun: the fly's bite gives sleeping sickness, a medical complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse fly spreads sleeping sickness, an illness or complaint in the medical sense.
